title: Chapter 63 — Multi-Threading
intro: Building multiple relationships inside a single trade account so the business survives any single contact change.

sections.title: The Single-Thread Risk
sections.content:
If your entire builder relationship runs through one project manager, what happens when that project manager leaves? You lose the account. Not because of performance — because of a personnel change.

Multi-threading means building relationships with multiple contacts inside the same account: the owner, the project managers, the site supervisors, the office admin who processes purchase orders. Each thread is an insurance policy against losing the account.

sections.title: How to Multi-Thread
sections.content:
Start with your primary contact. Ask for introductions: 'Would it be helpful if I met your site supervisor on the Riverside project? That way I can coordinate delivery directly without going through you for logistics.'

Attend their company events. Meet the owner at the HBA golf tournament. Introduce yourself to the office admin when you drop off a quote: 'I am the appliance rep — if you ever need anything for a project, here is my direct line.'

Send relevant information to multiple contacts. The product update goes to the designer. The rebate announcement goes to the project manager. The spec sheet goes to the site supervisor. Different value for different roles.

sections.title: Thread Maintenance
sections.content:
Track your contacts per account in CRM. Flag any account where you have fewer than two active contacts as 'single-threaded' and prioritize adding threads.

When a contact leaves, your other threads keep the account alive. When a new contact joins, your existing threads introduce you. Multi-threading is not just risk management — it is how accounts grow beyond a single relationship into an institutional partnership.
